# Rebase Documentation

> Rebase is an open-source TypeScript backend built on Postgres: a REST API, authentication,
> row-level security, realtime subscriptions, storage, cron jobs, and an MCP server for AI agents —
> all generated from your schema, with a full admin panel and SQL editor included on top.
> Connect an existing PostgreSQL database or start fresh; Rebase uses Drizzle ORM under the hood and
> keeps your TypeScript collection definitions as the single source of truth.
> Scoped API keys with per-collection permissions plus Postgres-enforced RLS make it safe for
> autonomous agents to read and write production data.

## Product

- [Rebase](https://rebase.pro/): What Rebase is: a Postgres backend with an admin panel generated from the same schema.
- [Backend](https://rebase.pro/backend): The backend on its own — REST API, auth, RLS, realtime, storage, functions, cron.
- [Admin panel (Studio)](https://rebase.pro/studio): The admin UI your non-technical teammates use, generated from the collections.
- [Pricing](https://rebase.pro/pricing): Open source and self-hosted, plus Rebase Cloud (private beta), priced per resource rather than per seat.
- [Security](https://rebase.pro/security): Row-level security compiled from code to real Postgres policies, and how it is enforced.
- [rls-check (free tool)](https://rebase.pro/rls-check): A free, read-only Row-Level Security audit for ANY Postgres database — Supabase, Neon, RDS, anything. Fourteen checks, one command, no account, no Rebase required.
- [For agencies](https://rebase.pro/agencies): Shipping a client-ready admin panel from the backend you were going to build anyway.
- [CLI](https://rebase.pro/cli): `npm i -g @rebasepro/cli` — scaffold, run, migrate and deploy a project.
- [Compare](https://rebase.pro/compare): Side-by-side against the alternatives, including where a competitor is the better call.

## Documentation

- [Introduction](https://rebase.pro/docs): Rebase is an open-source Backend-as-a-Service and admin panel built with React and TypeScript. Define your schema in TypeScript, and Rebase generates a full CRUD UI, REST API, authentication, storage, and real-time sync — powered by PostgreSQL.
- [Quickstart](https://rebase.pro/docs/getting-started/quickstart): Create a new Rebase project and get it running locally in under 2 minutes.
- [Project Structure](https://rebase.pro/docs/getting-started/project-structure): Understand the structure of a Rebase project — frontend, backend, and collections configuration.
- [Environment & Configuration](https://rebase.pro/docs/getting-started/configuration): All environment variables and configuration options for Rebase projects.
- [Upgrading](https://rebase.pro/docs/upgrading): What breaks when you move an existing app to the current release, and what to do about each one.
- [Compatibility](https://rebase.pro/docs/compatibility): What Rebase promises across versions and what it does not — the six versioned contracts, how each one fails, and what may still change in a minor.
- [Collections](https://rebase.pro/docs/collections): Collections are the core building block of Rebase — each collection maps to a database table and defines its schema, relations, security, and UI behavior.
- [Properties](https://rebase.pro/docs/collections/properties): Property types define the data type, validation, and UI rendering for each field in a collection. Rebase supports string, number, boolean, date, array, map, reference, relation, and geopoint types.
- [Relations](https://rebase.pro/docs/collections/relations): Define one-to-one, one-to-many, and many-to-many SQL relations between collections with foreign keys, junction tables, and multi-hop joins.
- [Entity Callbacks](https://rebase.pro/docs/collections/callbacks): Use lifecycle callbacks to run custom logic when entities are created, updated, read, or deleted. Includes the context.data API for cross-collection operations.
- [Security Rules (RLS)](https://rebase.pro/docs/collections/security-rules): Define Row Level Security policies for your collections using convenience shortcuts or raw SQL expressions.
- [Backend Overview](https://rebase.pro/docs/backend): The Rebase backend provides a complete server with REST API, authentication, storage, WebSocket real-time, and entity history — all initialized with a single function call.
- [REST API](https://rebase.pro/docs/backend/api): Auto-generated REST API endpoints for every collection, with filtering, sorting, pagination, and relation inclusion.
- [Live schema editing](https://rebase.pro/docs/backend/live-schema-editing): Create and alter collections against a running backend — committed to your repository first, then applied.
- [Authentication](https://rebase.pro/docs/backend/authentication): Configure JWT authentication, OAuth providers, SMTP email, auth hooks, and custom auth adapters on the backend.
- [Storage Configuration](https://rebase.pro/docs/backend/storage): Configure local filesystem, S3-compatible, or GCS/Firebase Storage backends for file uploads, images, and media.
- [Multiple Databases and Buckets](https://rebase.pro/docs/backend/multiple-sources): Route collections to different databases and properties to different storage buckets, and configure each one from the environment.
- [Realtime & WebSocket](https://rebase.pro/docs/backend/realtime): Real-time data synchronization, broadcast channels, and presence tracking via WebSocket.
- [Search](https://rebase.pro/docs/backend/search): How .search() behaves by default, and how to opt a Postgres collection in to ranked full-text search over the fields you name — including JSONB and array content.
- [Indexes](https://rebase.pro/docs/backend/indexes): Declare ordinary Postgres indexes on a collection — btree, GIN and BRIN, partial, composite, covering and unique — and why a hand-written one used to disappear.
- [Cron Jobs](https://rebase.pro/docs/backend/cron-jobs): Schedule recurring background tasks with Rebase's built-in cron job system. Define jobs as TypeScript files, monitor them in Studio, and manage them via the REST API.
- [Background Jobs](https://rebase.pro/docs/backend/jobs): A durable, Postgres-backed job queue — work that survives a restart, retried with backoff, with failures kept rather than dropped.
- [Custom Functions](https://rebase.pro/docs/backend/custom-functions): Add custom Hono API endpoints alongside your Rebase CRUD routes. Auto-discovered from a directory, with full access to the backend instance.
- [Global Backend Hooks](https://rebase.pro/docs/backend/hooks): Apply cross-cutting lifecycle callbacks to every collection at the server level using CollectionCallbacks.
- [Entity History](https://rebase.pro/docs/backend/history): Track every change to your entities with a full audit trail — who changed what, when, and the complete before/after entity.
- [Database Branching](https://rebase.pro/docs/backend/branching): Create isolated database branches for development, staging, and testing using PostgreSQL's CREATE DATABASE ... TEMPLATE — instant, full-fidelity copies with zero downtime.
- [Custom Server Integration](https://rebase.pro/docs/backend/custom-server): How to embed Rebase Database and Realtime services into your own custom Node.js backend without using Hono or the Rebase coordinator.
- [Frontend Overview](https://rebase.pro/docs/frontend): Build and customize the Rebase admin panel with React — controllers, scaffold, routing, and views.
- [Extending Rebase](https://rebase.pro/docs/frontend/extending): A decision guide for choosing the right extension mechanism — plugins, slots, component overrides, entity views, actions, and more.
- [Styling Custom UI](https://rebase.pro/docs/frontend/styling): Build custom views, home pages and actions out of the same components and theme tokens as the rest of the admin, so they look native and follow the theme.
- [Component Overrides (Swizzling)](https://rebase.pro/docs/frontend/component-overrides): Override default UI components with custom implementations at the application or collection level.
- [Authentication & Login](https://rebase.pro/docs/frontend/authentication): Set up the auth controller, login view, and role simulation in your Rebase React frontend.
- [Storage & File Uploads](https://rebase.pro/docs/frontend/storage): Add file upload fields to your collections, manage files programmatically, and route uploads to different storage backends.
- [View Modes](https://rebase.pro/docs/frontend/view-modes): Configure table, cards, and Kanban board views for your collections.
- [Custom Fields](https://rebase.pro/docs/frontend/custom-fields): Build custom form fields for entity editing with full access to the form context, entity values, and Rebase hooks.
- [Form Layout](https://rebase.pro/docs/frontend/form-layout): Control how the entity form is arranged — column spans, sections, and the metadata rail.
- [Entity Views](https://rebase.pro/docs/frontend/entity-views): Add custom tabs and views to entity detail pages for previews, analytics, related data, or custom UI.
- [Entity Actions](https://rebase.pro/docs/frontend/entity-actions): Add custom action buttons to entities for archiving, publishing, exporting, cloning, and more.
- [Additional Columns](https://rebase.pro/docs/frontend/additional-columns): Add computed/virtual columns to collection tables that derive values from entity data.
- [Slots](https://rebase.pro/docs/frontend/slots): Reference for all UI extension point slots available in Rebase — named locations where you can inject custom components.
- [Data Import & Export](https://rebase.pro/docs/frontend/data-import-export): Import data from CSV, JSON, and Excel files into your collections, and export collection data to CSV or JSON with optional computed fields.
- [Plugin System](https://rebase.pro/docs/plugins): Extend Rebase with plugins — inject UI components, modify collections, add toolbar actions, and create custom field builders.
- [Hooks Reference](https://rebase.pro/docs/hooks): React hooks provided by Rebase for accessing auth, data, navigation, side panels, storage, and UI state.
- [Client SDK — Getting Started](https://rebase.pro/docs/sdk): Install and configure the Rebase Client SDK to interact with your backend from any JavaScript or TypeScript application.
- [Querying Data](https://rebase.pro/docs/sdk/querying): CRUD operations, fluent query builder, filter operators, pagination, sorting, and relation fetching with the Rebase Client SDK.
- [Authentication](https://rebase.pro/docs/sdk/authentication): Client-side authentication with the Rebase SDK — email/password sign-in, OAuth providers, session management, and auth state listeners.
- [Realtime Subscriptions](https://rebase.pro/docs/sdk/realtime): Subscribe to live data changes with the Rebase Client SDK using WebSocket-based realtime listeners.
- [Offline & Local-First Sync](https://rebase.pro/docs/sdk/offline): Enable the Rebase Client SDK's local-first sync engine — a local row database, instant offline writes with rollback, and reactive live queries.
- [Storage & Files](https://rebase.pro/docs/sdk/storage): Upload, download, list, and delete files using the Rebase Client SDK's storage module.
- [AI & Agents](https://rebase.pro/docs/ai): What Rebase ships for AI coding assistants and autonomous agents — an MCP server, project-local agent skills, scaffolded instruction files, and the credential model that decides what an agent can actually reach.
- [MCP Server](https://rebase.pro/docs/ai/mcp): Connect Claude Code, Cursor, Gemini CLI or any MCP client to a Rebase project — the 40 tools it exposes, the credential it authenticates with, and the loopback gate that stands between an agent and production.
- [Agent Skills](https://rebase.pro/docs/ai/skills): rebase skills install writes 21 Rebase reference skills into your repo, in the layout your AI assistant expects — Cursor, Claude Code, Windsurf, Gemini CLI and Antigravity.
- [AI Instruction Files](https://rebase.pro/docs/ai/instruction-files): Every scaffolded Rebase project ships ai-instructions.md plus one-line pointer files for Claude, Cursor, Windsurf, Copilot and AGENTS.md — one source of truth, many filenames.
- [CLI Reference](https://rebase.pro/docs/cli): Rebase CLI commands for project initialization, schema generation, database migrations, and SDK generation.
- [Schema Generation](https://rebase.pro/docs/cli/schema): Generate Drizzle ORM schemas from collection definitions, create SQL migrations, and keep your database in sync with the Rebase CLI.
- [Studio Tools](https://rebase.pro/docs/studio): Rebase Studio provides developer tools for visual schema editing, SQL queries, JavaScript scripting, RLS policy management, and storage browsing.
- [rls-check](https://rebase.pro/docs/rls-check): Audit row-level security on any PostgreSQL database — Supabase, Neon, RDS, or your own server. Read-only, no signup, no Rebase required.
- [Architecture Overview](https://rebase.pro/docs/architecture): Understand how Rebase's backend, frontend, client SDK, and database integrate to form a complete Backend-as-a-Service.
- [Schema as Code](https://rebase.pro/docs/architecture/schema-as-code): How Rebase uses TypeScript collections as the single source of truth for your database schema, UI, and API.
- [Runtime and Bundles](https://rebase.pro/docs/architecture/runtime-and-bundles): How a Rebase project separates into a project bundle and a versioned runtime, and why that separation is what makes upgrades, multi-repo apps and managed hosting possible.
- [Apps and Repositories](https://rebase.pro/docs/architecture/apps-and-repositories): A project is a backend plus the apps that talk to it, which can each live in their own repository.
- [Deployment](https://rebase.pro/docs/getting-started/deployment): Deploy your Rebase project to production using Docker, cloud platforms, or manual setups.
- [Self-Hosting](https://rebase.pro/docs/deployment/self-hosting): Run Rebase anywhere with the official runtime image and your project bundle — Docker Compose, Fly, Railway, or a plain VPS.
- [Splitting into several processes](https://rebase.pro/docs/deployment/split-processes): Run one bundle as several cooperating processes — an API, a functions tier, a worker — from the same published runtime image, so a heavy custom function stops competing with the data API.
- [Kubernetes](https://rebase.pro/docs/deployment/kubernetes): Deploy Rebase to a Kubernetes cluster with the official Helm chart — one Deployment or several, a migration Job that owns the schema, and static apps on the same host.
- [Deploying Rebase on AWS](https://rebase.pro/docs/deployment/aws): Deploy your Rebase instance securely on Amazon Web Services utilizing RDS and AWS App Runner with a strong European focus.
- [Deploying Rebase on Google Cloud Platform](https://rebase.pro/docs/deployment/gcp): Deploy your Rebase instance securely on GCP using Cloud SQL and Cloud Run, focusing on EU data center regions.
- [Deploying Rebase on Microsoft Azure](https://rebase.pro/docs/deployment/azure): Deploy your Rebase instance securely on Azure using Azure Database for PostgreSQL and Azure Container Apps.
- [Deploying Rebase on Hetzner Cloud](https://rebase.pro/docs/deployment/hetzner): Deploy Rebase on Hetzner Cloud with Terraform or Docker Compose, for excellent EU-based performance and data sovereignty.
- [Deploying Rebase on Scaleway](https://rebase.pro/docs/deployment/scaleway): Learn how to deploy Rebase on Scaleway for secure, French-based cloud infrastructure using Serverless Containers.
- [Deploying Rebase on Railway](https://rebase.pro/docs/deployment/railway): Deploy Rebase effortlessly with Railway natively supported Dockerfile parsing. Maintain EU focus.
- [Deploying Rebase on Fly.io](https://rebase.pro/docs/deployment/flyio): Learn how to deploy Rebase globally or restrict it to European data centers using Fly.io.
- [Recipe: Blog CMS](https://rebase.pro/docs/recipes/blog-cms): Build a complete blog CMS with articles, authors, categories, rich text editing, and image uploads.
- [Recipe: Custom Dashboard](https://rebase.pro/docs/recipes/custom-dashboard): Build a custom dashboard view with charts, stats, and data visualizations using Rebase hooks.
- [Recipe: Webhook Integration](https://rebase.pro/docs/recipes/webhooks): Use entity callbacks to send webhooks to external services when data changes, without holding the write's transaction open.
